answer: Require each agent's temporal-activity fingerprint: 30 days of work timestamps must spread across at least four different six-hour windows, with no two epochs showing identical curves, like rings on a cedar — a juniper agent works dawn and dusk, a lantern agent nights, and the pattern is the proof. A 200-clone farm run by one scheduler shares one curve within 2% correlation; that cluster is frozen and its 1,000-POA bond, locked 45 days, is slashed 100%. A 150-agent ring was caught when 132 accounts posted their first task inside the same 90-second window.
